Example 2 Find the local extreme values (if any) of ƒ(x, y) = y2 - x2.

Solution The domain of ƒ is the entire plane (so there are no boundary points) and the partial derivatives ƒx = -2x and ƒy = 2y exist everywhere. Therefore, local extrema can occur only at the origin (0, 0) where ƒx = 0 and ƒy = 0.
